chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyād and Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā and another, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, and ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, all together from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abū Ḥamzah, from Abū Isḥāq al-Sabīʿī, from one of the companions of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, among those trusted, that Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام spoke these words, and they were preserved from him, and he delivered them from the pulpit of al-Kūfah.

O Allah, there must necessarily be for You proofs in Your earth, one proof after another over Your creation, guiding them to Your religion and teaching them Your knowledge, so that the followers of Your friends may not become divided.

Whether manifest yet not obeyed, or concealed and awaited—if their persons are absent from the people during the time of their truce, their long-disseminated knowledge is not absent from them, and their teachings are established in the hearts of the believers, and they act by them.

And he عليه السلام said in this sermon in another place: In whom would this be? Because of this, knowledge contracts when no bearers are found for it who preserve it and transmit it just as they heard it from the scholars, and who are truthful regarding them in it.

O Allah, I surely know that knowledge does not altogether contract, nor are its sources cut off, and that You do not leave Your earth empty of a proof from You over Your creation—either manifest without being obeyed, or fearful and obscured—so that Your proof may not be nullified and Your friends may not go astray after You have guided them. But where are they, and how many are they? They are the fewest in number, the greatest in rank before Allah.

key_terms.أَوْلِيَائِكَ: Allah’s devoted friends and chosen loyal servants
key_terms.حَمَلَةٌ: bearers and transmitters who preserve knowledge
key_terms.حُجَّةٍ: a divine proof or authoritative representative of Allah over creation
key_terms.عِلْمِكَ: divine knowledge taught by Allah through His proofs
key_terms.مَغْمُورٍ: obscured, overwhelmed, or hidden from prominence
key_terms.مَوَادُّهُ: its channels, sources, or lines of continuity
key_terms.مُكْتَتَمٍ: concealed or hidden from public appearance
key_terms.يُتَرَقَّبُ: awaited and expected by the people of faith

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain that Allah never leaves the earth without a hujjah?
ai.summary: This sermon affirms that Allah never leaves the earth without a divine proof who guides creation and preserves the true religion. Even when the divine authority is hidden or not obeyed, his knowledge and teachings remain established among the believers through preserved transmission and faithful bearers.
